market_question: Will Ethereum dip to $1,500 by December 31, 2026?
reasoning: Ethereum has strong demand from institutional ETFs and growing real-world asset tokenization, creating a floor around $2,000–$2,200. A drop to $1,500 would require a >40% decline, which is possible only in a severe bear market or black-swan event. While crypto remains volatile, the current macro and regulatory tailwinds make such a low-probability flash crash less likely than the market implies.
evidence_points: ETH has not traded below $1,500 since November 2022, with $2,000 acting as major support in 2023–2025.
Spot Ethereum ETFs have accumulated billions in inflows, providing a structural demand floor.
Historical one-minute flash crashes of >30% are rare and typically coincide with leveraged unwind events, not gradual bear trends.
sources_consulted: Ethereum ETF flow data (e.g., Farside Investors)
Crypto market structure reports from Q3 2025
